title: SummitBridge Onboarding Kickoff + KMS / SSO Review
summary: Kickoff for SummitBridge onboarding. Reviewed network topology (VPC peering vs private link), SSO/SAML flow, KMS key management, and pilot scope. Agreed to run a 2-week pilot on hosted Redwood with canary routing to Dedicated during peak loads. Next: send security pack, draft SOW, schedule runbook workshop and pilot benchmark window.
topics: Key management: KMS vs HSM, envelope encryption
Pilot design: hosted vs dedicated, latency targets, traffic shaping
transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-03-26 15:00 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jenna, Marco, Priya / Liam, Sofia, Rajesh

Summary (auto): Quick kickoff, security focus, clear pilot scope.

[00:00] Jenna Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Jenna from Redwood, AE on this account, Marco CSM and Priya our solutions engineer are on. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Liam O'Connor: Liam here, Head of Platform at SummitBridge. Sofia and Rajesh with me.
[00:12] Sofia Marin: hi all
[00:14] Marco Reyes: Hey Liam, thanks. we'll keep this to 45-60, try to get actions noted.
[00:18] Priya Natarajan: Quick agenda: network, identity/KMS, pilot topology, runbook and timeline. then Q/A.
[00:24] Rajesh Iyer: For us security first — SOC2 scope and K M S. also need audit logs and key custody answers.
[00:31] Jenna Patel: Totally, we'll cover how Redwood handles KMS integrations, HSM options for Private, and audit logs retention and export.
[00:38] Liam O'Connor: Our infra is in us-west-2, VPCs locked down, we prefer PrivateLink if possible but open to peering. we also have strict egress IPs for allowlist.
[00:49] Priya Natarajan: Ok noted. For hosted mode we support VPC peering and AWS PrivateLink — Private Link needs an endpoint in your account; peering is usually faster to stand up. There can be NAT egress nuances, and we do need a small set of outbound IPs for telemetry if allowlisting is required.
[01:05] Sofia Marin: When you say outbound IPs for telemetry, can you pin a range? our security team will only allow ranges, not CIDR / single IPs.
[01:12] Priya Natarajan: We can provide a /24 per region for dedicated pools, hosted has a small pool but we'll confirm exact ranges in the security pack.
[01:20] Rajesh Iyer: Can you describe key custody — do you hold the key or we provide KMS? we need key separation.
[01:27] Jenna Patel: You can bring your own key — Red wood integrates with customer K M S (KMS) or external H S M for Private. For hosted we have envelope encryption so we never store raw customer keys, and you can revoke access. we'll include the diagram in the docs.
[01:40] Liam O'Connor: Good. Also SSO — we use Okta with SAML and SCIM for groups. Role-based access is mandatory.
[01:47] Marco Reyes: We support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning. RBAC maps to roles in Console — we can map Okta groups to Redwood roles, and we have session timeout settings.
[01:57] Sofia Marin: Is there an audit trail? we need user-level audit logs for 1 year, exportable to our S3 or SIEM.
[02:05] Priya Natarajan: Yes audit logs — admin actions, token creations, model deployments, per-request traces available and exportable to S3 or Splunk via our connector. retention tiers vary; we'll include export examples.
[02:18] Liam O'Connor: Pilot question: we want to validate latency under normal and peak traffic, and also check for hallucination/regression on our prompt set. Target latency is <150ms for short queries (<128 tokens) and cost target is X per 1k tokens — can you show us how to measure both?
[02:34] Priya Natarajan: We'll instrument with per-request latency metrics and token billing breakdown in Console. For model quality we'll run your prompt set through Redwood Evals or use our compare-run to baseline. For latency we can do canary traffic split from your app to Redwood hosted, then push dedicated if it helps throughput.
[02:49] Rajesh Iyer: In dedicated mode how does network isolation work? do you see our traffic? do you manage the GPUs?
[02:56] Priya Natarajan: Dedicated pools are customer isolated; infrastructure controlled by Redwood but network path is private and we can deploy in a tenant-isolated VPC. we provide options for Azure/GCP/AWS depending on region. logs and metrics are accessible to customer.
[03:10] Marco Reyes: Note: we have SLA options for dedicated — 99.9% uptime and committed p99 latency tiers depending on the reserved size. we'll include pricing tiers.
[03:19] Sofia Marin: Ok. Data residency question: can we ensure tokens and data never leave us-west-2?
[03:25] Jenna Patel: For Private or Dedicated yes; hosted defaults to region selection and we can pin region for data residency. We'll document the region guarantees.
[03:33] Liam O'Connor: Timeline: we want pilot in two weeks, 2-week run, then production ramp in 6 weeks if all good. realistic?
[03:41] Marco Reyes: That's aggressive but doable — need SSO config, VPC connectivity and test prompts. If security review is quick, we can spin pilot in 10 business days.
[03:50] Rajesh Iyer: Security review will take 3-5 business days to triage docs, maybe longer for key agreements.
[03:55] Jenna Patel: We'll send the security pack today with K M S diagrams, SOC2 evidence, and an SOW template. Also a connectivity checklist for your infra team.
[04:03] Sofia Marin: Great. small nit: how do you handle token caching and kv cache — we need to understand privacy and retention for short-term caching?
[04:12] Priya Natarajan: Redwood uses prefix and KV caching for performance; cache is ephemeral and can be disabled for pilot. caching does not persist customer content to external stores and we can provide TTL controls. we'll include the caching behavior doc.
[04:26] Liam O'Connor: Any known limitations with large context windows? we have a few very long docs, sometimes 8k tokens.
[04:33] Priya Natarajan: We support long contexts; for best throughput we recommend chunking and streaming — kernel selection changes for long sequences and the runtime optimizes batch sizes. we'll propose quantization profiles depending on model.
[04:46] Rajesh Iyer: Who owns the runbook? we want to co-author so we know fallbacks.
[04:51] Marco Reyes: Redwood will provide a runbook template, SE will co-author with your SREs. it will include fallback policies (model variant fallback), routing, and escalation paths.
[05:02] Sofia Marin: Benchmarks — can we run a blast test to simulate peak? maybe a canary then surge.
[05:08] Priya Natarajan: Yes we can coordinate a controlled load test window with rate targets. we'll require a short ticket for scheduling to avoid noisy neighbor effects.
[05:17] Jenna Patel: Quick recap: deliver security pack + exact IP ranges, draft SOW, schedule runbook workshop (SE + your SREs), pilot window dates.
[05:26] Liam O'Connor: sounds good. also please include pricing for Dedicated commit vs hosted over the pilot period so we can compare.
[05:32] Marco Reyes: Will do — send a cost comparison with expected token volumes.
[05:36] Sofia Marin: One more: does Redwood support customer-managed logging ingestion? we prefer to ship logs into our Splunk.
[05:42] Priya Natarajan: Yes Splunk or S3 ingestion supported; recommend S3 export and then your pipeline pulls into Splunk — we'll add an example lambda.
[05:50] Jenna Patel: Any final Qs?
[05:52] Rajesh Iyer: none from me.
[05:54] Liam O'Connor: good, thanks all.

End meeting.

Notes: transcript has occasional mis-hearings (K M S spelled in audio as K-M-S sometimes), some speaker labels simplified.
